title: Drain Contract API + Autoscaler SLA Alignment for Tenant-Protective Upgrades
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: introduce a lightweight 'drain contract' API that formalizes a handshake between the upgrade orchestrator and the autoscaler so we can perform GPU pool upgrades with per-tenant capacity guarantees and bounded churn. This ticket scopes the API, controller lib, tests, and a minimal console view for rollout operators. Motivating problems: noisy upgrades cause tenant-level throttling and SLO violations because autoscaler treats drained nodes as capacity loss immediately. Existing staged-drain prototypes reduced impact but lacked a contract for temporary reservation and tenant-aware admission windows. The drain contract will let the orchestrator request short-lived grace tokens that autoscaler honors for scaling decisions, enabling safe eviction pacing, prioritized tenant padding, and explicit fallback behaviors.
background_and_rationale: We need a deterministic, observable protocol so upgrades don't regress customer latency or throughput. Current heuristic-based drains interact poorly with bursty autoscaling: autoscaler spins up new nodes which then quickly get drained and evicted, increasing churn and cost. A contract model decouples the intent (this node will be drained) from autoscaler policy (honor reservation or invoice fallback) and makes audit trails and rollout gates explicit for SRE/ops teams.
proposed_solution: 1) Define a protobuf DrainContract: { contract_id, pool_id, tenant_ids (optional), reserved_capacity_slots, start_ts, soft_deadline, final_deadline, priority_level }. 2) Implement a control plane controller that issues contracts during a rollout wave and exposes a REST endpoint and controller-runtime reconciler in the upgrade orchestrator. 3) Extend the autoscaler to consume contracts and adjust scaling decisions: treat reserved_capacity_slots as transient capacity (do not immediately scale up to replace). 4) Add enforcement hooks: if autoscaler cannot meet reservation before soft_deadline, orchestrator slows drains and triggers fallback (canary-safety / pause). 5) Add metrics (contract_issued, honored_count, missed_deadline, tenant_impact_by_contract) and a console panel with contract timeline and per-tenant risk score.
tradeoffs_and_alternatives:
- Conservative: keep using current heuristic drains (lower implementation cost but repeated regressions).
- Separate reservation service (service boundary) vs embedded controller (faster iteration). We prefer embedded for first iteration to reduce integration surface and latency.
- Full per-request admission gating (heavy) vs coarse contract slots (lighter). We choose the latter to preserve throughput and avoid per-request blocking.

acceptance_criteria: Autoscaler honors reservations in 95% of synthetic scenarios where capacity is available
Upgrade runbook includes steps to detect and recover from missed contract deadlines
No regression in p99 latency for top 10 tenants during staged rollout in perf test
Metrics emitted and visible in Console panel for issued/honored/missed contracts
testing_plan: Create a dedicated perf harness: 1) baseline run without contracts, 2) run with contracts and compare churn, scale events, and tenant p99 latency. Inject edge cases: autoscaler constrained by global quota, tenant hotspots, simultaneous multi-pool upgrades. Validate that orchestrator pauses drains when honor_rate < 0.9.
monitoring_and_alerting: New alerts: contract_missed_deadline_rate > 0.01 over 5m, contract_honor_rate < 0.95, tenant_latency_increase_during_contract > 20% for 2m. Dashboard: contract timeline + per-tenant impact heatmap + autoscaler decisions log.
rollout_plan:
- Feature flag gated: start as disabled in Dedicated staging, enable in 10% of pools (non-production tenants) for 1 week.
- Enable in 30% pools with operator on-call watching dashboards for 72h.
- Full rollout if no major regressions after 2 weeks.
- Fallback: revoke active contracts and revert to heuristic drains if severe regressions observed.
